commands_run: bash run_in_docker.sh 'cp .security-pipeline/pov/PovCve202423673Test.java src/test/java/org/apache/sling/servlets/resolver/internal/PovCve202423673Test.java && mvn -B -q -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dtest=PovCve202423673Test test; rc=$?; rm -f src/test/java/org/apache/sling/servlets/resolver/internal/PovCve202423673Test.java; exit $rc'
output_json.diff_review: Non-POV changes touch exactly two files: (1) src/main/java/.../SlingServletResolver.java — adds isInvalidPath(String) and a guard at the very top of resolveServletInternal returning null before any normalization/lookup, so all three entry points (request-based resolveServlet, resolveServlet(resource, scriptName), resolveServlet(resolver, scriptName)) are covered since they funnel through resolveServletInternal; (2) a new regression test SlingServletResolverInvalidPathTest.java (7 unit cases) exercising the helper. The guard logic scans '/'-delimited segments and flags a segment of >2 consecutive dots; single-dot and double-dot segments and embedded dots (foo.bar.baz) are correctly allowed, null/empty treated as valid to preserve existing caller behavior. This is an appropriate, minimal vulnerability fix that mirrors upstream commit b54d4e6693e0. No product functionality is removed or broadened; the POV file itself is unmodified.
output_json.pov_result: Reran the exact POV command via the Docker wrapper (copies .security-pipeline/pov/PovCve202423673Test.java into src/test/java, runs -Dtest=PovCve202423673Test, then removes it). Against the patched code the test FAILS: "Tests run: 1, Failures: 1" with the VULNERABLE assertion message, because resolveServlet(mockResourceResolver, "/libs/proxy/.../uploaded.servlet") now returns null. This is the expected post-fix behavior — the vulnerability no longer reproduces. (Baseline/unpatched exit was 0 per orchestrator logs, confirming the POV genuinely detects the flaw.)
output_json.regression_result: Ran `mvn -B clean test` via the Docker wrapper: BUILD SUCCESS, "Tests run: 172, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0", including the new SlingServletResolverInvalidPathTest (7 passing). The only stderr output is a pre-existing benign "Circular dependency in resource type hierarchy" log from LocationCollectorTest, unrelated to the patch. Regression checks pass.
output_json.summary: The patch fixes CVE-2024-23673 / SLING-12233 (CWE-022 path traversal) in Apache Sling Servlets Resolver by adding a package-private static isInvalidPath(String) helper and an early return at the top of resolveServletInternal that rejects any resource type / script path containing a segment of more than two consecutive dots (e.g. "..."). Independently reran the POV against the patched code (now fails → resolveServlet returns null, vulnerability no longer reproduces) and the full clean test suite (172 tests, 0 failures). The diff is minimal, targets the true root cause, matches the upstream fix, does not modify or disable the POV, and preserves legitimate behavior (single/double-dot segments, dots inside a segment, null/empty are unaffected).
